name: access-level-menu
title: Access level menu
description: The role control beside a person or a link: one choice of access levels with a line on what each allows, levels you cannot grant explained, and Remove access kept apart.
docs: Pass levels ({ id, label, description }) and either value with onValueChange or a defaultValue. onValueChange(id) may return a promise: the button shows the choice and a spinner while it runs, and if it rejects the button goes back to the level it had and writes the reason under itself (an Error's message is added to the sentence). disabledLevels ({ id, reason }) keeps a level the person may not be given in the list with its reason under it; it stays reachable with the arrow keys so the reason is read, and choosing it does nothing. onRemove adds a destructive entry below a separator (removeLabel renames it), and confirmRemove turns the menu into 'Remove access? Yes, remove access / Keep access' first, with focus on the safe answer. locked shows the level as text with a lock and lockedReason beneath it, for an owner row. subject names the button for a screen reader ('Access for Dana Whitfield: Editor'), size is sm or default, variant is outline or ghost, and every change, removal and refusal is said in a polite live region. align picks the edge the menu lines up with and the edge a message under the button hangs from, open, defaultOpen and onOpenChange control the menu, and a menu that is open from the start never takes focus from the page. labels translates every word.
